methodSources.title: Recommendations for application of the functional evidence PS3/BS3 criterion using the ACMG/AMP sequence variant interpretation framework.

authors.name: Clinical Genome Resource Sequence Variant Interpretation Working Group

methodSources.abstract: The American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG)/Association for Molecular Pathology (AMP) clinical variant interpretation guidelines established criteria for different types of evidence. This includes the strong evidence codes PS3 and BS3 for "well-established" functional assays demonstrating a variant has abnormal or normal gene/protein function, respectively. However, they did not provide detailed guidance on how functional evidence should be evaluated, and differences in the application of the PS3/BS3 codes are a contributor to variant interpretation discordance between laboratories. This recommendation seeks to provide a more structured approach to the assessment of functional assays for variant interpretation and guidance on the use of various levels of strength based on assay validation. The Clinical Genome Resource (ClinGen) Sequence Variant Interpretation (SVI) Working Group used curated functional evidence from ClinGen Variant Curation Expert Panel-developed rule specifications and expert opinions to refine the PS3/BS3 criteria over multiple in-person and virtual meetings. We estimated the odds of pathogenicity for assays using various numbers of variant controls to determine the minimum controls required to reach moderate level evidence. Feedback from the ClinGen Steering Committee and outside experts were incorporated into the recommendations at multiple stages of development. The SVI Working Group developed recommendations for evaluators regarding the assessment of the clinical validity of functional data and a four-step provisional framework to determine the appropriate strength of evidence that can be applied in clinical variant interpretation. These steps are as follows: (1) define the disease mechanism, (2) evaluate the applicability of general classes of assays used in the field, (3) evaluate the validity of specific instances of assays, and (4) apply evidence to individual variant interpretation. We found that a minimum of 11 total pathogenic and benign variant controls are required to reach moderate-level evidence in the absence of rigorous statistical analysis. The recommendations and approach to functional evidence evaluation described here should help clarify the clinical variant interpretation process for functional assays. Further, we hope that these recommendations will help develop productive partnerships with basic scientists who have developed functional assays that are useful for interrogating the function of a variety of genes.

experiment.title: Saturation Genome Editing of BARD1
experiment.shortDescription: We used saturation genome editing to measure the effect of 9,128 BARD1 SNVs and 2,048 3-base pair deletions on BARD1-dependent HAP1 cell survival.
experiment.abstractText: Systematic interrogation of the functional consequences of variants of uncertain significance (VUS) is critical to interpretation of clinical genetic testing. While some loss-of-function (LoF) mutations in the tumor suppressor BARD1 are linked to increased risk of inherited breast cancers, the overwhelming majority of variants in BARD1 have unknown impact. We applied Saturation Genome Editing (SGE) to assess 9,128 SNVs and 2,048 in-frame deletions for their effect of cell survival and RNA expression. We find that 13% of missense variants are LoF. SGE scores are highly concordant with ClinVar annotations, and LoF variants are significantly enriched in breast cancer cohorts. BARD1 SGE scores provide strong evidence for variant classification. We link SGE scores to BARD1 protein structure to link specific functions to BRCA1/BARD1 tumor suppression. Together, these results elucidate the clinical picture of BARD1 variation at both nucleotide and protein levels.

methodText:
Barcode reads were merged using PEAR and counted from merged FASTQ files, one per bin for each of the three replicates.

Data was analysed using CountESS.
abstractText: This study used variant abundance by massively parallel sequencing (VAMP-seq) to measure protein abundance using fluorescence in the Tuberin domain of TSC2. This assay identifies variants that are loss of function due to loss of abundance/stability.
shortDescription: Scores for the TSC2 Tuberin domain VAMP-seq assay analysed with the CountESS pipeline.

experiment.title: TSC2 Tuberin
experiment.shortDescription: VAMP-seq assay for the TSC2 Tuberin domain.
experiment.abstractText: This study used variant abundance by massively parallel sequencing (VAMP-seq) to measure protein abundance using fluorescence in the Tuberin domain of TSC2. This assay identifies variants that are loss of function due to loss of abundance/stability.
experiment.methodText: The variant library was ordered from Twist Biosciences and assembled into a plasmid along with the variant barcode. These plasmids were transfected into HEK293T cells containing a Bxb1 Tet-on landing pad for stable integration. Cells were sorted using FACS and barcodes from each bin were sequenced using Illumina. Barcode-variant associates were resolved using PacBio long read sequencing and analysed using Pacybara.

title: TSC2 RapGAP Domain Updated Scores
methodText:
Barcode reads were merged using PEAR and counted from merged FASTQ files, one per bin for each of the three replicates.

Data was analysed using CountESS.
abstractText: This study used variant abundance by massively parallel sequencing (VAMP-seq) to measure protein abundance using fluorescence in the RapGAP domain of TSC2. This assay identifies variants that are loss of function due to loss of abundance/stability.
shortDescription: Scores for the TSC2 RapGAP domain VAMP-seq assay analysed with the CountESS pipeline.

experiment.title: TSC2 RapGAP
experiment.shortDescription: VAMP-seq assay for the TSC2 RapGAP domain.
experiment.abstractText: This study used variant abundance by massively parallel sequencing (VAMP-seq) to measure protein abundance using fluorescence in the RapGAP domain of TSC2. This assay identifies variants that are loss of function due to loss of abundance/stability.
experiment.methodText: The variant library was ordered from Twist Biosciences and assembled into a plasmid along with the variant barcode. These plasmids were transfected into HEK293T cells containing a Bxb1 Tet-on landing pad for stable integration. Cells were sorted using FACS and barcodes from each bin were sequenced using Illumina. Barcode-variant associates were resolved using PacBio long read sequencing and analysed using Pacybara.
